Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

What we covered:
- High-level RTBF / deletion ask: ability for FintechCo to submit user-level deletion requests (API + portal) and for Redwood to remove associated model inputs/embeddings and request logs.
- Retention baseline: FintechCo currently enforces a 30-day active retention window, with backups/snapshots on a 90-day cadence. You flagged potential legal-hold scenarios for investigations.
- Residency: primary data is US; there may be EU-resident users in later phases.

Key questions we need from you to produce the SLA/draft:
1) Estimated volume: average number of deletion requests per month (or per day during peak).
2) Scope: confirm whether "delete" needs to cover raw inputs, embeddings, derived metadata, telemetry/logs, and search indices.
3) Legal hold policy: are there expected cases where FintechCo will place holds that require rolling back deletion for specific records?

What we can commit to / next steps from Redwood:
- I attached a short RTBF overview that shows our standard delete flow and typical purge timelines (primary store purge: 30 days; backups: up to 90 days depending on backup cycle).
- Connor will follow up with a draft RTBF SLA (we'll include accelerated purge options for Dedicated/Private customers).
- We'll confirm behavior for embeddings and KV caches and provide the API endpoints for programmatic deletes.

Requesting: if you can send an initial copy of your internal retention policy and the security questionnaire you mentioned (or the contact in legal), we'll incorporate specifics into the SLA draft.

Thanks — cc'ing Connor for technical/SLAs and Marissa for any SRE/SE follow-up.

Thanks Camila — appreciated the recap. A few answers and a couple of clarifications inline:

1) Volume: we expect ~200-300 deletion requests/month initially, with spikes up to ~1k/day if we roll out a self-service portal.
2) Scope: delete should cover raw user inputs we send to the model, any embeddings or derived vectors, and associated request metadata (timestamps, request IDs). We can live with anonymized telemetry for aggregate analytics but not with identifiable logs.
3) Backups/legal hold: our current policy requires that in normal operations backups can be retained up to 90 days; however, Legal may place case-by-case holds that require suspension of deletion for specific records.

Question: can Redwood provide an API that flags a record as 'deleted' and guarantees removal from primary store within 30 days and from backups within 90 days unless a legal hold is applied? Also: are embeddings immediately removed or marked for purge on the next reindex?

I've attached our retention policy and security questionnaire for reference.

Hi Sofia — thanks for the details. Quick technical summary to confirm expectations and call out options:

- API + Portal: Yes — Redwood supports programmatic deletes via our management API (DELETE /v1/customers/{id}/records) and via a secure UI for self-service. We record a delete request ID and provide callbacks/webhooks on completion.

- Primary store purge: standard SLA is to purge deleted records from primary storage within 30 days of request. This includes raw inputs and embeddings that are stored in the model-serving layer.

- Backups / snapshots: by default backups follow a 90-day retention cadence; purge from backups depends on the snapshot rotation schedule and can be up to 90 days. We can accelerate backup purges under contract for Dedicated/Private deployments, or if you agree to a short-term escrow/redaction plan for snapshots. Note: immediate removal from backups is technically constrained by immutable snapshot schedules and third-party storage lifecycle.

- Embeddings & indexes: embeddings are marked for deletion immediately and excluded from future indexing; physical removal happens on the next maintenance reindex/purge cycle (typically within 24–72 hours for active clusters, but final purging follows the primary-store SLA above).

- Legal holds: we support per-record hold flags; when a hold is applied, deletion for that record is suspended until cleared by FintechCo Legal. We'll surface hold counts and reasons in our Console and via API.

Action items / ask for SLA draft:
- Can you confirm the expected steady-state delete rate (200–300/mo) and peak (1k/day) so we can size retention and webhook throughput?
- Any EU-resident data in scope now or in the next 12 months? That affects residency and potential pseudonymization requirements.

I've attached a draft RTBF SLA for your review — it's a starting point and flags accelerated purge options (Dedicated/Private) and contract language for backup constraints.
